report.source_text: Postoperative CT scan showed the left thyroid lobe and the haematoma was excised. She was weaned off mechanical ventilation and extubated on the fourth postoperative day. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 10. On follow-up, the patient had complete resolution of compressive symptoms and hoarseness. The blood calcium results were in normal ranges after the partial thyroidectomy. Repeat neck ultrasonography after 1 month showed no mass in the neck.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old woman with ESRD on hemodialysis and a known nodular goiter presented with acute neck swelling, hoarseness, and progressive dysphagia, leading to respiratory acidosis due to hypoxia. Initial imaging (US and CT) revealed an enlarged, nonenhancing mass behind the trachea compressing the airway and esophagus. Endotracheal intubation was performed due to airway compromise, followed by urgent partial thyroidectomy. Postoperative histopathology confirmed multinodular goiter with spontaneous hemorrhage. The patient had a successful recovery, was extubated on postoperative day 4, discharged on day 10, and experienced complete resolution of compressive symptoms and hoarseness, with no mass detected on follow-up ultrasonography.
